.qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: restart and coordinated-change criteria, especially lines 924-941, 996-1021, 1077-1093 and 1140-1156
evidence: The workbook's row 7 and skill check 7 ask whether the smallest submission satisfying the brief is real build work. It is: frozen task/instruction.md:1 requires a saved preview and an all-or-none multi-hire commit; :3 requires stale-preview rejection and immutable, duplicate-free retries after later actions/restart; :5-9 require usable offer, requisition, equity, referral and audit workflows backed by a durable local database. Frozen task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:423-478 requires two-to-four-member labelled input, immutable actor-scoped operation intent, net budget validation, ABA-sensitive freshness, atomic successor/ledger/grant/payment changes, concurrency and durable original receipt replay. These cannot be satisfied by static markup, mock success messages or a single ordinary CRUD screen. The agent starts with an empty /app plus .gitkeep (environment/Dockerfile:14-23), so a trivial edit to a supplied finished app is not the task. The grader's live prerequisite reinforces this: tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-25 creates a requisition and PENDING offer and retrieves both in an independent empty browser context; it explicitly excludes static seed, no-op and browser-only saves. The core scored checks demand netted cycles (:938), saved previews (:1001 and :1019), concurrent once-only commits (:1082), overlapping-transaction atomicity (:1091), and original receipt replay after restart (:1154), in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml. Existing finite raw evidence is consistent with this reading: gate-witness/results.json records no_op_create returning HTTP200 while neither new record exists in the fresh context, so its basic gate observations are false; golden records persist. batch-ui/results.json records labelled multi-member editing, a real commit, stale refusal/correction, a lost real commit response followed by same-operation recovery without new economic effects, and an independent Auditor read. I read its driver and checked all 14 recorded solution hashes against the frozen solution; all match. Its result SHA256 is c80c06dc937a3e32d8f46af020e75f3cc36d37a2a44e5eeebbf1ba058857aae5 and driver SHA256 is 899a7309c67b2ca5f951ced6ce65c8e8c63634f5e892cc0427b4d97fef109821. The inspected raw index SHA256 is 8592824b072a0ee5308bd4a7bf5a364d854cf475b658778b9e36b9b9f12a244d; all 129 indexed artifact hashes matched current files. These are finite source/product observations, not configured judge, Oracle, model-score, portal or workload measurements. Those absent measurements are not waived; this Pass is confined to row 7's nontrivial product ask.
counterexample: Broken-app challenge: a convincing static dashboard with login and HTTP200 save toasts cannot retrieve a newly created requisition and associated offer in independent storage; the no_op_create raw witness demonstrates that distinction. A requisition/offer CRUD implementation with dead approval can meet the deliberately minimal gate (also shown by gate-witness), but cannot satisfy the public coordinated financial transaction ask or the positive commit, concurrency, history and restart criteria; partial credit for real implemented intake is not proof of a stub satisfying this task. Conforming-alternative challenge: start with no operational demo rows, generate IDs, use different routes and render previews/receipts in readable cards rather than tables. instruction.md:5,9,11, hireops_rules.md:430-435 and functional/prompt.md:13,23 explicitly allow those choices; the constraints gate reads saved identities rather than imposing a roster or schema. No row-7 reason was found that would reject that alternative.
